description: Transactions on bank, cash, PayPal and file-import check accounts (CheckAccountTransaction): value and entry dates, amount, payment purpose, payee/payer details, booking status and the owning check account. Incremental replication is available through the documented startDate filter, watermarked on valueDate. Because sevdesk documents no update-based or create-based filter on this operation (no updateAfter/createAfter parameter appears in its parameter list), that cursor is APPEND-ONLY: later mutations to already-replicated rows (status transitions 100->200->400, enshrining, PUT edits) are not re-emitted. Writes cover creation only - sevdesk documents POST /CheckAccountTransaction (create) and PUT /CheckAccountTransaction/{checkAccountTransactionId} (update by server-assigned id) as two separate operations, so no create-or-update mode can be grounded; the enshrine route is an irreversible side-effect action, not a write mode.

check_account_id.description: Retrieve all transactions on this check account (filters the record's checkAccount.id). Must be sent together with check_account_object_name.

check_account_object_name.description: Companion of check_account_id; sevdesk requires it only when check_account_id is provided. Use 'CheckAccount'.

is_booked.description: Only retrieve booked transactions (status 400). The spec does not name the record field this compares against.

paymt_purpose.description: Only retrieve transactions with this payment purpose.

payee_payer_name.description: Only retrieve transactions with this payee / payer.

start_date.description: Low-water-mark filter: only retrieve transactions from this date on. Declared by sevdesk as a date-time string on this operation (info.description's {timestamp} filter tables are written for Contact/Invoice/CreditNote and are not asserted for CheckAccountTransaction). GAP: the spec does not state which record field startDate compares against; valueDate is the reasoned mapping because it is the only always-present date field.

end_date.description: Upper bound: only retrieve transactions up to this date. sevdesk does not require it alongside startDate, so it is exposed as an ordinary stream filter rather than as the closing bound of a windowed cursor.

id.description: Transaction id; read-only, serialized as a JSON string on the wire (the write models declare it as an integer).

create.description: Creation timestamp (read-only). Provider-wide system field; wire values carry an explicit UTC offset (e.g. 2024-06-28T14:42:58+02:00).

update.description: Last-update timestamp (read-only). Provider-wide system field; wire values carry an explicit UTC offset. NOT usable as a replication cursor here - this operation exposes no updateAfter/updateBefore filter.

sevClient.description: Owning SevClient relation ({id, objectName='SevClient'}); read-only, auto-filled by sevdesk. Opaque JSON.

valueDate.description: The replication watermark. Non-nullable in the response model and required by the create model, so it is the only always-present date field on this resource. Wire values carry an explicit UTC offset (e.g. 2024-05-10T00:00:00+02:00). SPEC DEFECT (prose only): the response model describes it as 'date the transaction was imported' while the create/update models describe it as 'booked' - the descriptions are swapped between models; the type, format, sample and nullability are reliable.

entryDate.description: Second transaction date; wire values carry an explicit UTC offset. Nullable, which is why it cannot bound a cursor on every row. SPEC DEFECT (prose only): the response model describes it as 'booked' while the create/update models describe it as 'imported' - the descriptions are swapped between models.

amount.description: Amount of the transaction; a decimal serialized as a JSON string on read (the write models declare number/float). Negative for debits, e.g. '-100.32'.

payeePayerAcctNo.description: IBAN or account number of the payee / payer.

payeePayerBankCode.description: BIC or bank code of the payee / payer.

primaNotaNo.description: Prima nota number of the transaction.

checkAccount.description: The check account this transaction belongs to ({id, objectName='CheckAccount'}). Opaque JSON.

status.description: 100 = Created, 200 = Linked, 300 = Private, 350 = Auto-booked without user confirmation, 400 = Booked. Serialized as a JSON string on read; the write/update models declare it as an integer whose enum omits 350.

sourceTransaction.description: Source transaction of a money-transit / rebooking transaction ({id, objectName='CheckAccountTransaction'}); absent on ordinary transactions. Opaque JSON. The response model omits the nullable flag, but the create and update models both declare it nullable and scope it to money-transit transactions.

targetTransaction.description: Target transaction of a money-transit / rebooking transaction ({id, objectName='CheckAccountTransaction'}); absent on ordinary transactions. Opaque JSON. Same nullability sourcing as sourceTransaction.

enshrined.description: Timestamp at which the transaction was enshrined; unset until PUT /CheckAccountTransaction/{checkAccountTransactionId}/enshrine is called (irreversible, requires status 200 or higher). GAP: the spec carries no example for this field anywhere, so the type follows the connector-wide date-time ruling rather than a local sample.

schema.description: One transaction to create on a check account. sevdesk documents this route for check accounts of type 'online', preferably CSV-import accounts. Field types follow Model_CheckAccountTransaction (the write models), which differ from the read model: amount is a genuine number and status a genuine integer here, while both come back as JSON strings on read.

valueDate.description: Date of the transaction. Required on create.

checkAccount.description: The check account to create the transaction on. Required on create.

amount.description: Amount of the transaction (negative for debits). Genuine number on write, decimal-as-string on read.

status.description: 100 = Created, 200 = Linked, 300 = Private, 400 = Booked. sevdesk states that only status 100 makes sense when creating a transaction. Genuine integer on write, string on read; the write enum has no 350 (auto-booked), which is a read-only status.

payeePayerName.description: Name of the payee / payer. Listed in the create model's required array but declared nullable.

entryDate.description: Second transaction date. Optional on create.

payeePayerAcctNo.description: IBAN or account number of the payee / payer.

payeePayerBankCode.description: BIC or bank code of the payee / payer.

sourceTransaction.description: Source transaction, for money-transit / rebooking transactions only.

targetTransaction.description: Target transaction, for money-transit / rebooking transactions only.
